summary: Adds three endpoints: a user search by name, a per-key request counter, and an upstream status probe. It also registers these endpoints in main.go.

findings.title: Search query built from request input
findings.problem: Search pastes the name query parameter straight into the SQL text with fmt.Sprintf. The database then runs whatever SQL the caller supplies.
findings.consequence: Any caller of GET /users can read or change every row in the database.
findings.fix: Pass name to QueryContext as a bound parameter instead of formatting it into the SQL text.
findings.suggested_change: rows, err := h.DB.QueryContext(r.Context(), "SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE name = ?", name)

findings.title: Mutex left locked on missing key
findings.problem: Count locks h.mu and then returns early when the key is empty. That early return never unlocks h.mu.
findings.consequence: One request without a key leaves h.mu locked for good. Every later Count request then hangs forever.
findings.fix: Check the key before taking the lock, or unlock with defer right after Lock.

findings.title: Response body closed before error check
findings.problem: fetchStatus defers resp.Body.Close before it checks err. When http.Get fails, resp is nil and the deferred call dereferences it.
findings.consequence: Each failed upstream request panics the handler. The client then gets a dropped connection instead of the intended 502.
findings.fix: Move the deferred close below the error check.

findings.title: New handlers have no covering test
findings.problem: This change adds the Search, Count and Upstream handlers. The repository has no test files that cover them.
findings.consequence: Bugs like the stuck lock and the nil response go unnoticed until production.
findings.fix: Add httptest-based tests for each handler, including the empty key and unreachable upstream paths.

dropped.reason: This hit flags the same formatted query that the c1 finding already covers.
